description: Public repositories the dogfood harness scans, pinned to exact commits. The pin is the point: without it the baseline moves whenever upstream lands a dependency bump, and a real regression in this tool becomes indistinguishable from somebody else's commit. Chosen for shape rather than fame, so that every lockfile format the scanner claims to read is exercised, including the absence of one.

repos.skipNote: workspaces/arborist/test/fixtures/conflict-package-lock/package-lock.json is a deliberately broken npm lockfile (not valid JSON). Every npm lockfile is read at any depth since 0.11.0 and one that does not parse stops the scan whatever ignorePaths says, so no bench config can clear it. Until 0.15.0 the first broken manifest (workspaces/arborist/test/fixtures/bad/package.json) stopped the scan before lockfiles were read and hid this one; 0.15.0 collects every manifest parse failure and lets a lockfile parse error keep its own code.
repos.shape: npm workspaces monorepo with a v3 package-lock; the format with full coverage, at the size where transitive entries dominate
pnpm workspace, many packages, exercises onlyBuiltDependencies in place of the install-script flag pnpm stopped recording
pnpm workspace with a different package layout to vite's, and catalog specifiers
yarn berry, single package; manifest-level checks only, since berry records no resolved URL
yarn workspace monorepo under lerna, so the manifest walk has many roots
no committed lockfile; the scan has to say what it could not check rather than report clean

repos.configNote: eslint does not carry these ignorePaths entries upstream and has no .dep-guard.json of its own. The bench applies them so the repository can be measured: the two fixtures are deliberately broken package.json files (not valid JSON), neither is a project (no lockfile, workspace pattern or reference names it), and dep-guard stops on an unparseable stray manifest unless ignorePaths covers it. Findings under these two directories are filtered as a result. The paths are the whole manifest-parse listing of a 0.15.0 scan at the pinned commit.
repos.shape: no committed lockfile at a size where the manifest alone carries a long dependency list
small, no lockfile, few dependencies; the cheap end of the range

Python project with a pyproject.toml and a uv.lock and no npm lockfile at the root, so the Python manifest and lockfile surface has a baseline; the lockfile one-hot records JavaScript formats only and reads none here
small Django project whose requirements/ directory chains files together with -r includes
Python requirements files with -r ../ and -c constraint chains, a real broken include, and tag-pinned git requirements
small uv workspace whose members come from a packages/* pattern
uv workspace with explicit members plus an npm subproject; pins the SHA-pinned PEP 508 git dependency fixed in 0.16.1
pnpm workspace with real symlinks outside its workspace patterns

repos.skipNote: Fixture lockfiles in the repository are npm v3 lockfiles with no packages map, which dep-guard reads at any depth and stops on as a lockfile parse error, so no bench config can clear it.
repos.shape: monorepo carrying many fixture lockfiles, one of which stops the scan

repos.skipNote: The template's pyproject.toml contains template syntax and is not valid TOML, so the scan stops with a manifest parse error (exit 2) beside the repository's lockfiles.
repos.shape: templated pyproject beside lockfiles; a manifest that cannot be parsed
